promptLatex: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. The acute angle at the upper intersection measures $35^{\circ}$. An obtuse interior angle at the lower intersection, in degrees, is $m$. What is $m$?
hintLatex: The angle you want is the supplement of an angle you can already name.
The angle at the lower intersection corresponding to the given one also measures $35^{\circ}$.
That angle and the required one form a linear pair, so $m = 180 - 35 = 145$.
solutionLatex:
At the upper intersection the acute angle is $35^{\circ}$, and its vertical angle is also $35^{\circ}$.
Corresponding angles are congruent, so the angle at the lower intersection in the same relative position also measures $35^{\circ}$. That angle and the required interior angle lie on one side of the transversal and together make a straight line, so they are supplementary.
Therefore $m = 180 - 35 = 145$.
